channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Programa de renegociação de dívidas está pronto para ser anunciado após volta de Lula ao Brasil, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the federal government's debt renegotiation program is ready and will be announced after President Lula's return to Brazil. The program will use Treasury guarantees to encourage banks to offer better terms to debtors, without affecting the Union's primary spending.

item.title: Governo admite transição para fim da escala 6x1, mas descarta desoneração
item.description: The government admits the possibility of including a transition period for ending the 6x1 work schedule, but ruled out new tax breaks to compensate employers. Minister José Guimarães said President Lula plans to announce the reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours in May, Workers' Month. Furthermore, the bill regulating app-based work will be voted on only after the elections due to lack of consensus among platforms, workers, and the opposition.

item.title: Assessor de Marçal que deu soco em marqueteiro grava vídeo com Flávio
item.description: Nahuel Medina, an aide to candidate Pablo Marçal who punched publicist Duda Lima during the 2024 São Paulo mayoral debate, posted a video alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The video was published on Thursday, April 16, 2026, amid the 2026 election campaign. The gesture highlights alliances between far-right factions and Bolsonaro-linked figures.

item.title: 'Queremos que a escala 6x1 acabe já', diz Boulos sobre projeto de Lula
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos said he wants an immediate end to the 6x1 work scale proposed by the Lula government, advocating for a 90-day transition period for companies to adapt, rejecting the five-year timeline suggested in the CCJ as 'postponement'. He also discussed the bill regulating app-based work, defending a minimum payment of R$10 per trip as a fair inflation-adjusted reimbursement for motorcycle couriers.

item.title: Tarcísio nega que saída de ex-chefe da PM foi motivada por citação em investigação da Corregedoria
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas denied that the change in command of São Paulo’s Military Police was motivated by the mention of former chief Coronel José Augusto Coutinho in a Corregedoria investigation into alleged links with the PCC and the Transwolff bus company. He stated Coutinho requested to leave for personal reasons and praised his impeccable record, noting such rotations are common and that the new commander, Coronel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli, was selected for her distinguished career. Coutinho’s defense claims he has not accessed the investigation files and reiterates his integrity, while the São Paulo government refuses to comment on ongoing Corregedoria proceedings due to legal secrecy.

item.title: Após vitória na Alerj, Douglas Ruas diz que falará com Ricardo Couto e STF sobre linha sucessória no estado
item.description: Douglas Ruas, elected president of the Alerj by the PL, announced he will inform acting governor Ricardo Couto and the STF of his victory to discuss the state's succession line. He stated that, if he assumes command, he intends to build upon and improve measures taken by the current president of the TJ-RJ, describing the situation as 'totally atypical'. His election has raised questions about judicialization to secure the succession, with the PL already filing a request with the STF.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas divide integrantes do governo Lula
item.description: Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães expressed support for repealing the 'blusinhas' tax, acknowledging it harms President Lula’s popularity. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin countered that no government decision has been made, defending the 20% levy on international purchases under $50, arguing total import taxes remain lower than those on domestic production. The issue exposes a rift in the Lula administration, with economic officials backing the tax and political allies pushing for its removal.

item.title: Zanin e Moraes votam para manter cassação de Rodrigo Bacellar
item.description: Minister Cristiano Zanin voted to deny a legal appeal by the defense of former state deputy Rodrigo Bacellar (União-RJ), upholding the TSE's decision that revoked his mandate and declared him ineligible. The First Chamber of the STF followed Zanin's vote, confirming the rejection of the request to suspend the effects of the removal.

item.title: O Preço do Futuro (Parte 1)
item.description: Prediction markets offer a real-time mechanism to gauge expectations about future events — such as elections, interest rates, and inflation — by converting probabilities into tradable contract prices. In the Brazilian context, these markets could reveal market confidence in the Copom’s decisions, inflation trajectory, political risk, and international credibility, especially amid global volatility. Extending this logic to Brazilian politics would enable precise tracking of informed bets on electoral outcomes and policy shifts, turning news into market conviction signals.

item.title: ‘Médico dos presidentes’, Roberto Kalil Filho é eleito membro titular da Academia Nacional de Medicina
item.description: Cardiologist Roberto Kalil Filho, known as the "doctor of presidents," was elected a titular member of the National Academy of Medicine with 72 out of 96 votes, occupying Chair No. 01. He emphasized the institution's relevance to society and noted his role as physician to President Lula. His career includes over 300 scientific publications and leadership roles at FMUSP, Sírio-Libanês, and InCor.

item.title: Moraes vota por condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro a um ano de detenção por difamar Tabata
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to convict Eduardo Bolsonaro to one year of detention in an open regime and 39 days-fine for defamation against Deputy Tabata Amaral. Moraes stated that Bolsonaro falsely accused Tabata of intending to illicitly benefit third parties through her bill on public distribution of sanitary pads, acting with full awareness of the offensive nature of his posts. The vote was delivered in the STF’s virtual plenary, with the session set to conclude on April 28.

item.title: Lula fala em regulação digital para barrar interferência externa em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for digital regulation to prevent foreign interference in Brazil's 2026 elections, speaking a day before a meeting with other progressive leaders. He also offered self-criticism regarding the global rise of extremism, emphasizing threats to democracy.

item.title: Fachin critica relatório da CPI que mirava ministros do STF, mas nega crise institucional com Senado
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Edson Fachin criticized the Senate Organized Crime CPI report calling for the impeachment of STF ministers and the Attorney General, arguing judicial decisions should be challenged through appeals, not institutional attacks. He denied an institutional crisis between the Judiciary and Legislature, stating there are only interpretive disagreements on the scope of CPIs, and stressed that both branches must uphold their prerogatives while subjecting parliamentary work to public scrutiny.

item.title: Lula alerta que, quando democracia retrocede, 'acontece um Hitler'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva warned that democratic backsliding can lead to the emergence of figures like Hitler, urging the strengthening of democracy at international gatherings such as the one held in Barcelona this Saturday, attended by leaders including Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

item.title: Zema volta a criticar STF e Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) renewed his criticism of the Brazilian Supreme Court and Justice Gilmar Mendes in posts on X throughout April 2026. He accused the minister of making decisions based on personal favors, referenced alleged R$129 million contracts for Mendes’ wife, and stressed that judicial rulings must follow the Constitution. Zema also defended his own actions at the STF to address inherited debts and questioned the legitimacy of favorable rulings for Minas if perceived as concessions.

item.title: Fachin diz que que perde-se a confiança sempre que juiz ‘parece estar atuando como agente político’
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin warned that public trust erodes when judges are perceived as political agents disguised as legal interpreters, stressing the need for separation of powers and fidelity to the Constitution. He emphasized that in a representative democracy, elected legislators—not judges—should define public policy, and that the judiciary cannot impose personal preferences as functional decisions.

item.title: ‘Pesquisa é fotografia de um momento’, diz Marina Silva sobre liderança ao Senado em SP
item.description: Marina Silva emphasized that her lead in Senate polls for São Paulo reflects only a current moment and should not be seen as definitive. She attributed her performance to her political trajectory, including presidential candidacies, federal deputy service, and her work as Minister of the Environment, highlighting progress in reducing deforestation and restoring Brazil’s international credibility. Marina stated she aims to bring to the Senate an agenda that integrates environmental preservation with economic development, moving beyond prohibitions to present concrete solutions.

item.title: Três em cada dez brasileiros apostam dinheiro em bets, diz pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: A Genial/Quaest survey found that 29% of Brazilians over 16 engage in online sports betting (bets), with the highest rates in the South (37%), among men (33%), and those earning 2–5 minimum wages (32%). Bolsonarists (33%) and Catholics (34%) show the highest prevalence, while Lula supporters (26%) and evangelicals (23%) have the lowest.

item.title: Violência política de gênero corrói a democracia, diz Janja
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva denounced that gender-based political violence corrodes democracy and disproportionately affects women during her speech at the 'No to war, no to political violence: for an ecofeminist world' meeting in Valencia, Spain. She emphasized the urgency of expanding dialogue spaces among female leaders to confront armed conflicts, ecological crisis, and inequalities, stating that when one woman advances, none are left behind. President Lula is also in Europe, beginning a six-day trip through Spain, Germany, and Portugal to seek support for the Mercosul-EU agreement.

item.title: CCJ terá sessão na próxima semana para votar PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) of the Chamber of Deputies has scheduled a session for next Wednesday at 2:30 p.m. to vote on a PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work schedule. Rapporteur Paulo Azi read the opinion supporting the proposal’s admissibility, but a collective view request from the opposition delayed analysis; Chamber President Hugo Motta adjusted the schedule to allow voting next week. If approved in the CCJ, the proposal will proceed to a special committee before plenary vote, aiming for passage by the end of May, as aligned between Motta and President Lula.

item.title: Paulo Guedes critica 'afrouxamento' fiscal do atual governo e diz ter 'zero chance' de entrar na política
item.description: Paulo Guedes criticized the current government's fiscal loosening, saying it pressures inflation and prevents lower interest rates. He stated he has 'zero chance' of entering politics but assessed that the right is favored to win Brazil's 2026 presidential elections, without mentioning Flávio Bolsonaro. Guedes also noted the West is undergoing a geopolitical reassessment, with rearmament and migration control becoming more relevant due to public dissatisfaction with weak growth and comparisons to China.

item.title: Caixa diz analisar oportunidade no mercado de apostas de quota fixa
item.description: Caixa Econômica Federal has abandoned plans to launch the 'Caixa bet' in 2026, postponing the initiative to 2027 if at all. The state-owned bank states it is continuously analyzing opportunities in the fixed-odds betting market, aligned with government guidelines, without signed contracts or penalty obligations. The decision reflects technical, legal, and sustainability criteria, amid President Lula's opposition to betting.

item.title: Lei cria cargos e funções para o Tribunal Regional Federal com sede no Recife
item.description: The Federal Regional Court of the 5th Region, headquartered in Recife, will gain three new judges, 32 effective judicial analyst positions, 25 judicial technician roles, and 57 commissioned positions under Law 5.393/26, signed by President Lula. The measure addresses rising judicial workload in the region, covering six Northeastern states. The law originated from Bill 4278/25 of the STJ, approved by the National Congress.

item.title: A aposta religiosa de Flávio Bolsonaro para tentar acelerar vantagem nas pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is targeting Catholic voters, traditionally aligned with the PT, through institutional outreach to the CNBB and a moderated discourse emphasizing family and social stability. Although the PT still holds an advantage among Catholics, the campaign sees opportunity due to shifts in this electorate toward conservative positions and away from centrist alignments. The strategy aims to erode Lula's historical advantage in a tight race where small voter shifts in key segments could be decisive.

item.title: 'Tenho muitas preocupações no Brasil para me preocupar com a Venezuela', diz Lula na Espanha
item.description: During a press conference in Barcelona, President Lula stated he would not deepen his involvement in the Venezuelan crisis due to Brazil's domestic priorities, emphasizing that Venezuela must resolve its issues without foreign tutelage. He recognized the legitimacy of Vice President Delcy Rodríguez as president following Nicolás Maduro's arrest, noting the constitutional succession was valid and that any decision on new elections rests with the Venezuelan people.

item.title: Zanin e Moraes votam para manter cassação de Bacellar determinada pelo TSE
item.description: Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Cristiano Zanin voted to uphold the electoral cassation of Rio de Janeiro deputy Rodrigo Bacellar, imposed by the Superior Electoral Court for abuse of political power in the 2022 elections. Bacellar, currently imprisoned, sought to suspend the decision to avoid an indirect gubernatorial election, but the STF denied the request, maintaining the conviction for misuse of public infrastructure to hire electoral operatives.

item.title: Sem adversários, Douglas Ruas é eleito presidente da Alerj
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) was elected president of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislature (Alerj) in an election marked by opposition boycott and lack of competitors, receiving 44 favorable votes. The vote occurred after the withdrawal of the opposition-backed candidate and despite judicial challenges to the process’s legitimacy, including the annulment of a prior election in March. Ruas, an ally of former governor Cláudio Castro and a pre-candidate for the Guanabara Palace, assumes office amid political instability, with the president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice, Ricardo Couto, retaining executive authority per STF ruling until a successor governor is selected.

item.title: Brasil e Espanha assinam acordos sobre big techs e tecnologia digital
item.description: Brazil and Spain signed agreements in Barcelona on cooperation regarding big techs, digital technology, strategic minerals, and combating inequality and discrimination. The agreements cover collaboration in IT, telecommunications, SMEs, cultural exchange, sustainability, air transport, and social security, with emphasis on regulating large tech firms to prevent 'digital colonialism'. Lula highlighted Spain’s historical investments in Brazil, exceeding US$10 billion across 50 partnership projects, and stressed the need for digital sovereignty through joint efforts between supercomputing centers.

item.title: Motta quer votação da PEC do fim da escala 6 X 1 no plenário até julho
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta stated that the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule will be voted on in the CCJ next week, with the goal of approval in the plenary before the July recess. He denied accusations of delay, arguing that the PEC format allows for deeper debate, despite the Lula government's constitutional urgency bill. The PEC requires a 3/5 supermajority and will proceed to a special committee after CCJ approval before reaching the plenary.

item.title: Debate sério não observa só tamanho da carga tributária, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that a serious debate on Brazil's fiscal situation must examine the composition of the tax burden, not just its size, which has hovered around 32% of GDP since the early 2000s and remains below the OECD average of 34.1%. He noted that under the Lula administration, income tax has gained prominence in primary revenue due to measures targeting offshore accounts, JCP taxation, foreign dividends, and closing tax loopholes, increasing progressivity. Durigan also emphasized that the 2022 primary surplus was inflated by temporary factors and that Brazil's core issue is not high taxation, but the unequal distribution of who bears the tax burden.

item.title: Lula assina memorando com Espanha e impõe controle de minerais críticos
item.description: President Lula signed a memorandum of understanding with Spain on critical minerals, emphasizing joint development of the supply chain and domestic processing in Brazil as part of a national sovereignty strategy. The agreement avoids repeating the export-only model of iron ore and bauxite, prioritizing internal value addition and conditioning exports to domestic needs. The federal government rejects state-level deals with the U.S. as unconstitutional and seeks to align negotiations with Canada and other partners on three pillars: non-discrimination, processing in Brazil, and priority to internal consumption.

item.title: Novo presidente da Alerj entra na linha sucessória e assume como governador do Rio? Entenda
item.description: The new president of the Alerj, Douglas Ruas (PL), entered the state’s gubernatorial line of succession but did not assume the executive office due to a court decision maintaining Ricardo Couto, president of the TJ-RJ, as acting governor after Cláudio Castro’s resignation. Judge Suely Lopes Magalhães rejected the PDT’s request for a secret vote in the Alerj’s Mesa Diretora election, stating that the voting format falls under the legislative house’s organizational autonomy. The definitive successor to Castro will be determined by the STF’s ruling on the indirect election model for governor and vice-governor.

item.title: Defensoria diz que Moraes violou direito de defesa de Tagliaferro ao nomear órgão para o caso
item.description: The Public Defender's Office has asked the Supreme Federal Court to annul Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to appoint a public defender for Eduardo Tagliaferro, a former aide of Moraes at the TSE, arguing it violates the right to defense as Tagliaferro was not personally summoned to appoint new counsel after his lawyers were removed. Tagliaferro's lawyers state his address in Italy has been in the case files since October 2025 and that service by edict was unlawful, especially since the DPU acknowledges he did not abandon the case. The DPU urges adherence to legal procedures so Tagliaferro may choose new defense, or, if the appointment stands, that procedural deadlines be reopened.

item.title: Douglas Ruas (PL) é eleito presidente da Alerj e deixa Governo do RJ sob dependência do STF
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), pre-candidate for Governor of Rio de Janeiro, was elected president of Alerj with 44 votes, while 25 deputies walked out in protest and one abstained. The election reflects polarization in the legislature and raises concerns about governability, as the state government now depends on STF rulings to advance controversial agendas.

item.title: Saiba como votou cada deputado na eleição que definiu Douglas Ruas como novo presidente da Alerj
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) was elected the new president of the Alerj with 44 out of 45 votes, while one deputy abstained. The election took place after obstruction by the group of Rio Mayor Eduardo Paes, whose party (PSD) boycotted the vote along with 24 other legislators. Although Ruas won, the election was later annulled by judicial decision following the TSE’s removal of Governor Claudio Castro and former Alerj president Rodrigo Bacellar, sparking a succession dispute now under review by the STF.

item.title: Douglas Ruas é eleito novo presidente Alerj em sessão marcada por obstrução do grupo de Paes
item.description: Douglas Ruas of the PL was elected president of the Alerj with 44 votes, despite obstruction from Eduardo Paes's group, which saw 25 lawmakers absent from the vote. The session featured protests, left-wing lawmakers booing the result, and chants of 'diretas já' outside the chamber. Ruas defended the legitimacy of the process and the House's autonomy, while the opposition said it will appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Lula cita 2 números sobre feminicídio na Espanha: “Imprensa sabe o que foi”
item.description: During a press briefing in Spain, President Lula cited two conflicting figures regarding the reduction of femicide in the country — 75% and 30% — acknowledging the inconsistency and stating that the press would know the correct number. He praised Spain's progress in combating gender-based violence, highlighted the memorandum of understanding signed with Brazil, and mentioned that First Lady Janja had contact with a victim protection system that could be adopted in Brazil.

item.title: 'Espero que veto seja derrubado', diz Motta sobre PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) advocates for overturning the presidential veto on the sentencing dosimetry bill related to the January 8 attacks, which aims to review excessive punishments without granting amnesty. He states the bill was developed with jurists, technicians, and judiciary representatives to prevent a new institutional crisis, and expects Congress to reject President Lula’s veto, set for review on April 30.

item.title: “Espero que o veto ao projeto da dosimetria seja derrubado”, afirma Motta
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) advocated for overturning President Lula’s veto on the dosimetry bill, which reduces sentences for those convicted of the 2023 coup attempt. He said the bill aims to ease tensions between branches of government and prevent a new institutional crisis, clarifying it is not an amnesty but a Penal Code change allowing defense teams to request sentence reductions from the STF. Motta also stressed that the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule is not meant to delay voting but to ensure broad discussion on reducing working hours.

item.title: STF retoma em 28 de abril julgamento que pode tornar Malafaia réu por ataques a generais do Exército
item.description: The STF will resume on April 28 the judgment of the PGR's complaint against pastor Silas Malafaia, accused of slander and libel against Army generals. Rapporteur Justice Alexandre de Moraes has already voted to accept the complaint, citing sufficient evidence of materiality and authorship of the statements made in April 2025. If the majority accepts the complaint, Malafaia will become a defendant and the case will proceed to the evidentiary phase.

item.title: Moraes vota para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro à prisão, em julgamento no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to convict former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro to one year in prison in an open regime for defaming Congresswoman Tabata Amaral. Moraes claimed Eduardo insinuated that Amaral sought to benefit a businessman when introducing a bill. The trial is taking place in the virtual plenary, and Moraes justified imprisonment by stating Eduardo is in an 'uncertain and unknown location', preventing alternative measures.

item.title: PDT tenta suspender na Justiça nova eleição para presidente da Alerj
item.description: The PDT filed a lawsuit in Rio de Janeiro’s court to suspend the election for the presidency of the Alerj scheduled for Friday, citing failure to comply with the 5-day deadline for slate registration and insufficient time for minority organization. The party also challenges holding the vote before the STF defines the state’s succession line, arguing the 'swift' election seeks to interfere with ongoing institutional determinations. PDT deputy Vitor Junior is running against PL’s Douglas Ruas, who seeks to regain leadership after his prior election was annulled.

item.title: Moraes vota para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata Amaral
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to convict former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against congresswoman Tabata Amaral, proposing a sentence of one year detention and 39 day-fines (over R$80,000) over a 2021 social media post alleging her bill on intimate pads served a company lobby. The vote noted the crime was committed against a public official due to her functions and via social media with vast reach, and stated that alternative penalties cannot apply as Bolsonaro is in an unknown location (USA).

item.title: Lula: afrouxamento das regras de posses de armas levou a desvios que beneficiaram criminosos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the loosening of gun ownership rules in Brazil, stating that it benefited criminals. He said those who relaxed the regulations now want to 'outsource' the fight against organized crime to other countries, without directly naming the Bolsonaro administration.

item.title: Lula sacrifica debate do fim da escala 6×1 ao fazer populismo eleitoral com a proposta
item.description: Lula proposed ending the 6×1 work scale as an electoral strategy to reverse declining popularity, despite knowing it has little chance of passing Congress due to the election year, sectoral resistance, and legal risks. The proposal, criticized by experts and entities like the CNI, could raise business costs, increase unemployment, and push workers into informal labor without wage compensation. Lula will likely blame Congress and 'elites' for the failure, maintaining a 'us vs. them' narrative to mobilize his base.

item.title: Ex-comandante da PM de SP foi citado em inquérito da Corregedoria que apura atuação de empresa de ônibus ligada ao PCC; veja vídeo
item.description: The former commander-general of São Paulo's Military Police, Colonel José Augusto Coutinho, was cited in a Corregedoria investigation for attempting to dissuade a police officer suspected of working for Transwolff — a bus company linked to the PCC — from leaving the elite Rota unit. Seven officers allegedly participated voluntarily in the scheme, which included escorting company executives and receiving payment in illicit funds for money laundering. Coutinho's departure was formalized by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, who appointed Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli as the first woman to lead the force in nearly 200 years, a move seen as politically strategic ahead of the 2026 election, where public security will be a central campaign theme.

item.title: Na Espanha, Lula critica big techs e fala em “colonialismo digital”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized big tech companies in Barcelona, warning that without regulation, they are creating a 'digital colonialism' by extracting and monetizing data to concentrate power in the hands of a few billionaires. He called for expanding platform regulation, citing the ECA Digital as a first step, and stressed the need to protect Brazil’s sovereignty, especially during an election year, to prevent foreign interference. Lula also announced bilateral cooperation with Spain on supercomputing and AI, and condemned the 'industry of lies,' including hate speech and disinformation online.

item.title: ‘Tenho muita preocupação no Brasil para me preocupar com a Venezuela’, diz Lula na Espanha
item.description: President Lula stated during the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit in Barcelona that Brazil should not directly interfere in Venezuela's political affairs, emphasizing that his focus remains on domestic challenges. He defended respect for Venezuelan sovereignty, asserting that Venezuelans themselves must decide their country's future, including whether to call elections, and said the Brazilian government does not seek a leading role in the process. While avoiding intervention, Lula expressed a desire for stability and well-being in Venezuela, reaffirming Brazil's principle of non-intervention in international crises.

item.title: Lula diz que afrouxamento das regras de posse de armas levou a desvios que beneficiaram criminosos
item.description: President Lula stated that the loosening of gun possession rules in Brazil, enacted during Bolsonaro's government, led to deviations that benefited criminals. He criticized those who promoted the measure and now seek to outsource the fight against organized crime to other countries, referencing the U.S. initiative to label factions like PCC and CV as terrorist organizations. Lula also noted that the number of progressive leaders worldwide is declining, during his participation in the Democracy Always Forum in Spain.

item.title: Lula diz que fará acordo sobre minerais críticos com todos os países que quiserem negociar com o Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will establish agreements on critical minerals with all countries willing to cooperate, announcing a partnership with Spain on rare earths. He emphasized the defense of national sovereignty over mineral wealth, declaring that no one will own Brazil’s mineral resources. Lula also defended Venezuela’s right to self-determination, asserting that its political future should be decided solely by Venezuelans.
